column1: # Authored expectation for the Phase-3 host-assertion surface join.
# `development_plan_gate_integrity.md` section S clause 2 requires the run to enumerate
# its test surfaces and join them **completely** to an independently authored
# expectation. This file is that expectation, and nothing in it is generated: the check
# ids are read off the Phase-3 contract's Gate integrity section, the mutant ids off the
# committed records under `test/mutant/host_assert_cli/`, and the command topology off
# `substrate_doctrine.md` section 6 plus this phase's Sprint 3.2 deliverables.
# The join is two-way and total. A check the gate decides that no surface claims fails
# the gate, and a surface claiming something the run did not produce fails it too. That
# is what stops a deleted check or a quietly dropped command from shrinking the gate.
# The `# command` rows below are the second half of the same idea, and they are read by
# `tools/host_assert_cli_gate.py` rather than by a human: each names one command path,
# the options it carries, and whether it is consumer or maintainer surface. The gate
# joins them against the parser's own introspection in both directions, so a command
# gaining an option, losing one, or appearing at all is a failure until this file says
# so. Authored from the contract -- an emitter that wrote its own expectation would
# prove only that it is consistent with itself.
# command pb admin dhall update | --probes | consumer
# command pb admin kv delete |  | consumer
# command pb admin kv get |  | consumer
# command pb admin kv list |  | consumer
# command pb admin kv put | --value-stdin | consumer
# command pb admin vault init |  | consumer
# command pb admin vault unseal |  | consumer
# owner is the registry the ids are enumerated from at run time:
#   checks    the check ids tools/host_assert_cli_gate.py decides
#   mutants   the committed records under test/mutant/host_assert_cli/
#   commands  the command paths the Click parser enumerates at run time
